findings.rationale: Feature means of WA shift abruptly at round 11: the shift in federation SDs is about 0 through round 10 and jumps to about 0.4-0.6 SD from round 11 on, with the largest shift on AgeGroup/GenHlth/HighBP. The drift summary flags WA's mean shift (z=+3.7). The same onset round and the same feature family appear in NE and UT, so this may be a shared drift event; WA's own shift is the most precisely measured because it is the largest client. Other screens for WA (performance, updates, subgroups) are unremarkable, so the evidence rests on the drift tables alone.

NE's feature distribution is stable through round 10 (shift_sd 0 at round 10) and moves to about 0.39 SD at round 11, then stays between 0.37 and 0.67 SD for the rest of training (AgeGroup, then GenHlth and HighBP). The onset matches WA and UT. NE's client-level mean shift is large (0.24), and it has a moderately elevated update norm, but its performance is normal.

UT's feature shift is near 0 through round 10 and jumps to about 0.45 SD at round 11, then stays between 0.45 and 0.71 SD through round 20 (GenHlth, HighBP, AgeGroup). This is the largest mean shift in the federation (0.28). The onset matches WA and NE, which suggests a common drift event. UT's local performance and subgroups are normal, so the evidence is limited to the feature drift.

report.summary: Screens covered all 52 clients: updates (c2), local performance (c3), drift (c4), feature tails (c5), and subgroup outcomes by Sex, AgeGroup and Income (c6-c8), with a confirmation drift pass on WA, NE and UT (c9). The budget is fully spent (0 left). The main signal is a feature-distribution drift beginning at round 11 in three large clients (WA, NE, UT), all on the same features (AgeGroup, GenHlth, HighBP). I reported these as drift with moderate confidence, since the shared onset suggests a common event and the evidence rests on the drift tables. I found no evidence of poisoning, free-riding, label noise, prevalence shift, subgroup under-diagnosis or explanation instability. Weaker leads that I did not report: CT (GenHlth upper tail, z_noise 5.8, with normal performance), WV (MentHlth tail, z_noise -5.3, uncorroborated), GU (small client; CITL z=-3.7 and median norm z=3.2), and several small-group AgeGroup/Income subgroup outliers that have small n. Given the budget limit, I could not confirm these further.
